messages.author: e6ecea3c19f2ad0f
messages.subject: Setup RHadoop on CDH
parts:
I have a working CDH 4.3.0 cluster running on Amazon EC2's Ubuntu 12.04 LTS. I would like to use RHadoop on that cluster.

I have been using the following commands to install R and rmr2 on each node in the cluster:

sudo add-apt-repository 'deb http://cran.rstudio.com/bin/linux/ubuntu precise/'
sudo apt-key adv --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com --recv-keys E084DAB9
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install r-base r-base-dev

sudo R CMD javareconf

sudo R
install.packages(c('Rcpp', 'RJSONIO', 'itertools', 'digest'), repos="http://cran.revolutionanalytics.com", INSTALL_opts=c('--byte-compile') )
install.packages(c('functional', 'stringr', 'plyr'), repos="http://cran.revolutionanalytics.com", INSTALL_opts=c('--byte-compile') )
install.packages(c('rJava'), repos="http://cran.revolutionanalytics.com" )
install.packages(c('randomForest'), repos="http://cran.revolutionanalytics.com" )
install.packages(c('reshape2'), repos="http://cran.revolutionanalytics.com" )
install.packages('bitops')
install.packages('functional')
q()

sudo apt-get install git

git clone git://github.com/RevolutionAnalytics/rmr2.git
sudo R CMD INSTALL --byte-compile rmr2/pkg/


I have also added the following lines to the beginning of /etc/profile

export HADOOP_HOME=/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH-4.2.1-1.cdh4.2.1.p0.5/lib/hadoop
export HADOOP_CMD=/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH-4.2.1-1.cdh4.2.1.p0.5/bin/hadoop
export HADOOP_STREAMING=/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH-4.3.0-1.cdh4.3.0.p0.22/lib/hadoop-0.20-mapreduce/contrib/streaming/hadoop-streaming-2.0.0-mr1-cdh4.3.0.jar

When I run sudo R and then require(rmr2), those commands work and the necessary packages are loaded in R.
However, when I try to test it, using:    test = to.dfs(1:10000), it says:

Error in hadoop.cmd() : 
  Please make sure that the env. variable HADOOP_CMD or HADOOP_HOME are set

I have used sudo su - hdfs to get into the hdfs user and can see the environment variables from there.

Any idea what I am doing wrong?

messages.author: 63023c771a070260
messages.subject: Re: Setup RHadoop on CDH
parts:
sudo won't export your environment by default. You have to use the -E option. You can check that by calling

sys.getenv("HADOOP_CMD") 

at the R prompt just before your to.dfs test.

The -E option is considered not-so-secure. Just don't run sudo R, if you have to you are doing something else wrong.


Antonio
